rules.summary: The cap on critic rounds per feature (in EVO, per increment), counting every review path.
searches: grep -rniE 'rounds?|cap' <paths>: read each hit about critic or review rounds

rules.summary: The default review level (R1 for SDD and EVO) and Critical features always at R2.

What each review level runs (R0 no critic, R1 one critic, R2 the cycle) and which levels have a critic. Naming the levels (names) next to a pointer to the source, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy; what a level runs is always a copy outside the source.
searches: grep -rnE '\bR[012]\b' <paths>: read each hit that says what a level runs

rules.summary: Review level with the depth gate off or under a standing acceptance: a raise applies and is reported, a lowering is asked; a standing acceptance covers only the default.
fingerprints: \blevel you recommend and the programmer validates\b
searches: grep -rniE 'raise|lower|standing acceptance' <paths>: read each hit about the review level

rules.summary: DIRECT runs a clean critic only when the programmer asks for one.
As executor at R1, a second critic on the fixes runs only if the programmer asks.
A later critic round reports only Blocker and Major findings in the diff since the previous round.
Hard stops stop the feature in every gate profile.
searches: grep -rniE 'hard stop|every (gate )?profile|any profile' <paths>: read each hit that says what stops regardless of the profile

rules.summary: Which events are hard stops: a mention outside the source names one only with a pointer to protocols/gates.md §Hard stops (or the bare protocols/gates.md, or §Hard stops) in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters before or after it.
searches: grep -rniE 'hard stop|stops? (the feature )?(always|regardless|whatever)' <paths>: read each hit that names an event as a hard stop

rules.summary: When the critic-round cap is reached with a Blocker or Major finding of any round still open, the feature stops and asks the programmer. What counts as open is always a copy outside the source; naming the stop (names) next to a pointer to the source, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not.
searches: grep -rniE 'cap|rounds? run out|(blocker|major)[^.]*open' <paths>: read each hit about what happens when the critic rounds end with findings open

rules.summary: Commits made after the last critic round (its fixes included) are listed with their hashes as unreviewed before acceptance, never presented as reviewed. Naming them as unreviewed (names) next to a pointer to the source, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
fingerprints: \bthe fixes of (?:that|the last|the final) round included\b
searches: grep -rniE 'unreviewed|not (been )?reviewed|after the last (critic )?round' <paths>: read each hit about commits that no critic saw

rules.summary: In auto, a decision that chooses which of two or more rules the author wrote prevails stops the feature and goes to the programmer; what counts as a rule the author wrote (not the behavior of code). Naming it (names) next to a pointer to protocols/gates.md §When a gate is off, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
rules.pointer: protocols/gates\.md ?§ ?when a gate is off|§ ?when a gate is off
searches: grep -rniE 'rules? (the author|you) wrote|written by the author|authored rule|contradict[^.]*rules?|decided by agent' <paths>: read each hit about who settles a choice between written rules in auto

rules.summary: When an agent is resumed and when a relay replaces it: the per-model token caps, the 100k band, what a point follow-up is, and the usage thresholds read from subagent_tokens. Naming the cap (names) next to a pointer to SKILL.md §4 Reusing agents, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy; a number or a threshold is always a copy outside the source.
searches: grep -rniE 'resum|relay|replac|subagent_tokens|[0-9]+ ?k\b|follow-up' <paths>: read each hit that says when an agent is resumed or replaced

rules.summary: The relay: the outgoing agent is resumed for one turn to write relay notes (exploration only, no diffs, contents or logs) under the git common dir; the orchestrator writes them when it cannot; the new agent reads the notes and the full diff. Naming the relay notes or their folder (names) next to a pointer to protocols/context-handoff.md §Relay, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
searches: grep -rniE 'relay|one turn|notes' <paths>: read each hit about how a same-role replacement starts

rules.summary: Pause versus stop everything: on a pause running agents finish and no new delegation starts; on stop everything they are stopped at once and their IDs recorded; the resume state lists finished, interrupted and to-relaunch work, and interrupted work is relaunched, never assumed done. Naming stop everything (names) next to a pointer to SKILL.md §7, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
searches: grep -rniE 'paus|stop (everything|all)|running agents|interrupted|relaunch' <paths>: read each hit about what happens to running agents when work stops

rules.summary: In auto, a catch-up in the SKILL.md §5 shape goes to the programmer unasked at each phase or increment transition; the move into acceptance counts, the start of the feature does not; the auto increment report takes that shape. Naming the catch-up next to a pointer to SKILL.md §5, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
fingerprints: \bstart of the feature (?:does not|doesn't|adds no|is not)\b
searches: grep -rniE 'catch-up|transition|increment report|as a report' <paths>: read each hit about what the programmer is told unasked in auto
